themes_detail.label: Boiler crisis accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK—a 167% jump from the 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.67)—suggesting a concentrated heating failure problem affecting multiple buildings in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens as winter deepens.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (167% spike, z-score 5.67)
Heat/hot water is the 2nd largest complaint category overall (925 complaints in 90 days), indicating structural vulnerability
Timing aligns with winter weather and increased heating demand
reporting_angles: Interview affected tenants about lack of heat; check if complaints cluster around specific buildings or landlords
Investigate whether landlords are deferring boiler maintenance; cross-reference with DOB permit data (1,213 filings in 90 days, mostly alterations)

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure degradation spike
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped 227% to 18 THIS WEEK (vs. 5.5 weekly average), overgrown tree/branch complaints hit 10 (up 281%), and traffic complaints surged 357% to 8—signaling rapid deterioration of street conditions and vegetation management across the district in the last 7 days.
evidence: Curb condition: 18 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.5 weekly average (227% spike, z-score 3.95)
Overgrown tree/branches: 10 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (281% spike, z-score 3.58)
Traffic complaints: 8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (357% spike, z-score 3.81)
Street Condition is 3rd overall complaint category (594 complaints in 90 days)
reporting_angles: Walk problematic blocks to document deteriorating curbs, potholes, and overhanging branches; identify if a specific street or zone is worst-hit
File FOIL request for DPR and DOT maintenance schedules to determine if the district is under-resourced relative to complaints

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement activity surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 500% to 3 THIS WEEK (from 0.5 weekly average, z-score: 3.54), suggesting either a new enforcement blitz or emerging street vending conflicts in the district.
evidence: Vendor enforcement complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Signal is recent and isolated, suggesting a discrete event or policy shift rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Check NYPD precinct logs and SLA enforcement actions this week; determine if NYPD or Parks Enforcement is conducting a targeted vendor sweep
Interview street vendors about any new enforcement activity or citations; check if complaints center on food carts, merchandise vendors, or other type

themes_detail.label: Commercial disposal problems emerging
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints spiked 700% to 3 LAST WEEK (vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score: 5.42), suggesting a new waste-handling problem, possible illegal dumping, or non-compliance among local businesses.
evidence: Commercial disposal complaints: 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Complaint type is rare (0.4 baseline), making a cluster of 3 statistically anomalous
No corresponding spike in broader 'Dirty Condition' category (318 complaints over 90 days), suggesting localized commercial issue
reporting_angles: Map the 3 complaints to identify whether they cluster around a restaurant district, commercial corridor, or specific businesses
Contact DSNY to determine if any businesses were cited for improper waste management or if illegal dumping was reported

themes_detail.label: Green taxi activity spike unexplained
themes_detail.summary: Green taxi complaints jumped 700% to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score: 5.42), indicating either a surge in illegal green-cab activity or a recent policy change affecting their operations in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: Green taxi complaints: 3 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Complaint type is historically very rare, making this cluster a statistical outlier
Signal is 2 weeks old (not this week), suggesting it may have already resolved or is not currently escalating
reporting_angles: Contact TLC to determine if there was a policy change, surge in illegal green-cab dispatches, or specific incident two weeks ago
Map complaints to see if they're clustered near transit hubs (Prospect Park, major avenues) or residential zones
